attempts.response: {"ideas":[{"title":"Narrative is the recurrent locus of pipeline drift — run a controlled upstream-boundary trial focused on Narrative","description":"Across Experiments 007–009 the Narrative stage is the most frequent first point where a company-first introduction shifts into a product- or orchestration-led story or where unsupported audience/validation claims appear. This idea matters because it focuses scarce experimentation capacity on the stage most often implicated by the evidence, increasing the chance of a clear, diagnostic result that distinguishes whether the problem is Narrative framing (vs Idea, Synthesis, or Compose). It is supported by the report’s recommendation to run a single controlled upstream-boundary trial and by the per-run localization tables. Gaps/uncertainty: causation is not established — Narrative’s role may be upstream-influenced in some runs (Synthesis/Idea sometimes start the drift), so the trial must preserve identical upstream inputs to isolate Narrative’s effect.","evidence":"Experiment 007: Narrative is first visible drift in candidate runs 001–002; candidate 003 shifts at Synthesis but Narrative inherits the break. Experiment 009: Narrative is the first clear hierarchy shift in baseline 002/003 and in candidates 001–003; several examples in the report show Narrative inventing unsupported audiences or elevating orchestration to company direction.
